title: Human augmentation technologies are transforming healthcare,rehabilitation, industrial ergonomics, assistive living, sports, and personal mobility by improving human capabilities and enhancing quality of life.
description:
• Description Students are required to conceptualize a Human Augmentation device or assembly of their choice using Autodesk Fusion. The design should reflect original thinking and real-world engineering intent. The proposed solution may address applications in healthcare, rehabilitation, industrial ergonomics,assistive living, sports, or personal mobility, and may include (but is not limited to):
• Exoskeleton Mechanisms
• Prosthetic Components
• Rehabilitation Devices
• Assistive Support Systems
• Ergonomic Enhancement Products
• Wearable Assistive Devices
• Adaptive Mechanical Aids From the complete assembly, participants shall identify one critical machinable mechanical component that is strictly manufacturable using either Subtractive 3-Axis CNC Milling or Subtractive 2-Axis CNC Turning.The selected component shall be clearly identified within the complete assembly, indicating its location and function in the Human Augmentation product. Participants shall also justify why the selected component is suitable for the chosen CNC manufacturing process.Using Autodesk Fusion, participants shall develop the complete digital manufacturing workflow for the selected component, including:
• CAD Modelling
• Manufacturing Setup
• Tool Selection
• Toolpath Generation
• Machining Simulation
• Toolpath Optimization
• G-code Generation The final solution should demonstrate good engineering design practices, manufacturability, machining efficiency, and effective use of Autodesk Fusion CAD/CAM capabilities.
• Expected Outcomes The proposed solution should include:
• CAD model of the identified critical mechanical component within the assembly.
• Justification for selecting the component for either Subtractive 3-Axis CNC Milling or Subtractive 2-Axis CNC Turning.
• Manufacturing setup and machining strategy.
• Toolpath generation and machining simulation.
• Optimized manufacturing process.
• Product renders (assembled and exploded views).
• Participation Guidelines For Idea Submission
• Each student team shall submit a PowerPoint Presentation (6–8 Slides) describing their proposed Human Augmentation solution.
The presentation should include:
• Problem statement and proposed solution.
• Concept sketches.
• CAD model of the identified critical mechanical component within the assembly.
• Assembly view highlighting the selected CNC-manufactured component.
• Justification for selecting the component for either Subtractive 3-Axis CNC Milling or Subtractive 2-Axis CNC Turning.
• CAM workflow developed in Autodesk Fusion, including:
• Manufacturing Setup
• Tool Selection
• Toolpath Generation
• Machining Simulation
• Toolpath Optimization
• Product renders (assembled and exploded views).
NOTE: Physical machining or prototype fabrication is not required during the Idea Submission stage. Teams will be evaluated based on the proposed design,CAD model of the identified critical mechanical component, component selection, and digital manufacturing workflow demonstrated in Autodesk Fusion.
• Designs should be created using ONLY Autodesk Fusion and not copied or taken from any other source.
• AI Generated content is NOT ALLOWED.
For Grand Finale*: Students must use Autodesk Fusion to design and manufacture specific components to machine size within the given time period and present the following to the jury members:
• PPT explaining the final project
• Final Manufactured components
• Public link of the design
• Rendered images NOTE: *Grand Finale details to be revealed on competition day.
• The required 3-Axis CNC Milling Machine and 2-Axis CNC Turning Machine will be provided by the organizers during the Grand Finale.
• Attach Marking Criteria Table and Reference Workflow here*
• Faculty (SIH SPOC) Form Teams choosing to submit idea for Autodesk’s problem statement are required to request their faculty (SIH SPOC) to fill this 'Mandatory Form'
• Autodesk Fusion
• Autodesk Fusion is a cloud-based 3D modeling, CAD, CAM, CAE, and PCB software platform for professional product design and manufacturing.
• Students and educators can click here to get FREE access to Fusion.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a medtech / biotech / healthtech problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): addresses a more targeted user group within MedTech / BioTech / HealthTech. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (2/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Human Augmentation Device Design and CNC Manufacturing Workflow (Autodesk Fusion Design Challenge)

overview.in_plain_terms: Design (not build) a human augmentation device, an exoskeleton component, prosthetic part, or assistive device, and develop a complete CNC manufacturing plan for one key machinable component, using Autodesk Fusion.
overview.why_it_matters: This tests genuine mechanical design and manufacturing-process thinking for assistive technology, real skills needed to actually get devices like this from concept to physical reality.
pain_points: Human augmentation device concepts often aren't developed with a genuine manufacturing pathway in mind.
Bridging from a design concept to an actual CNC-machinable component requires real process planning.
No standard demonstration exists connecting assistive-device design intent to real manufacturing feasibility.
overview.background: This is an Autodesk-sponsored concept design and CNC manufacturing workflow challenge, not a software build or working device, requiring Autodesk Fusion for both design and manufacturing-process planning.
overview.whats_being_asked: Conceptualize a human augmentation device/assembly, identify one critical CNC-machinable component, and develop the complete digital manufacturing workflow for it using Autodesk Fusion.
expected_solution: One identified, justified CNC-machinable critical component.
Complete digital manufacturing workflow (toolpaths, setup, process planning) for that component.
Documentation of design and manufacturing rationale.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Design/CAD submission format, evaluated on design creativity, real-world engineering intent, and genuine CNC manufacturing process understanding, not software functionality.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Effort goes into CAD design and CAM (computer-aided manufacturing) workflow development within Fusion, a distinct skillset from coding.

competitive_landscape.level: Low crowding among typical hackathon teams
competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine CAD/CAM and mechanical design skill, a different pool of participants than most PS in this dataset.

innovation.note: Judged on design creativity and genuine real-world engineering intent, not algorithmic novelty.

invention.note: Judged on CAD/CAM workflow quality and manufacturing-process understanding.

technical_feasibility.note: Achievable within 36 hours for a team with real Fusion CAD/CAM experience; not achievable without it.

impact_and_benefits.note: About demonstrating genuine design-to-manufacturing capability for assistive technology.

architecture.note: Not applicable in the software sense, this is a mechanical design and manufacturing-process deliverable.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Same framing as SIH26112, only viable for a team with genuine Autodesk Fusion CAD/CAM experience, specifically manufacturing workflow development, not just modeling.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very clear, well-specified deliverable requiring genuine justification for component and manufacturing-process choices, real engineering-judgment demonstration.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without real CNC/CAM workflow experience specifically (beyond basic 3D modeling), the manufacturing-workflow half of this deliverable will be weak or absent.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm real, hands-on experience with Fusion's CAM (manufacturing) workspace specifically, not just modeling, this PS explicitly requires a full digital manufacturing workflow, not just a 3D model.

idea_0_4: Confirm team Fusion CAM proficiency specifically; if none, do not pursue this PS.
Choose your human augmentation application area and sketch a concept with real engineering intent.
Split: one person on the full assembly concept design, one on identifying and detailing the CNC-machinable component.
prototype_4_22: Model your complete human augmentation device/assembly concept in Fusion.
Identify and justify your critical machinable component (why this component, why this CNC process).
Begin the manufacturing workflow: stock setup, toolpaths, machining strategy for your chosen 3-axis milling or 2-axis turning process.
integration_22_30: Complete your CAM workflow with realistic toolpaths and machining parameters.
Validate your manufacturing approach against real machinability considerations (tool access, fixturing, tolerances).
Document your design and manufacturing rationale thoroughly.
polish_30_36: Prepare clean renders of your full assembly and detailed views of your machinable component.
Prepare your CAM workflow documentation/simulation showing the manufacturing process.
Rehearse explaining both your design intent and your manufacturing-process reasoning.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show a genuine CAM toolpath simulation for your component with realistic, justified machining parameters, not just a pretty 3D render, that manufacturing-process depth is the actual differentiator this challenge is testing for.

strengths: Very clear, well-specified deliverable requiring genuine engineering justification.
Real, valuable application domain (assistive technology) if design intent is thoughtful.
weaknesses: Completely inaccessible without genuine Fusion CAM (manufacturing workflow) experience specifically.
Requires both design creativity and real manufacturing-process engineering knowledge together.

roles_needed: Mechanical/CAD designer with Fusion CAM experience (mandatory)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS is not viable without genuine Fusion CAM proficiency, a hard prerequisite.
team_fit.approach: Confirm CAM-specific tool proficiency before committing, modeling skill alone isn't sufficient for this PS's manufacturing-workflow requirement.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Not applicable, this is a CAD/CAM design deliverable requiring real hands-on tool skill.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The entire design and manufacturing-process planning, genuine mechanical and manufacturing engineering judgment that AI tooling doesn't substitute for.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Not applicable in the typical sense, but attempting this without real CAM proficiency would produce an incomplete or unconvincing manufacturing workflow.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, this is a design and manufacturing-process-skill challenge.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, if the team lacks Fusion CAM proficiency, this PS should not be selected.

judge_qna.question: Why did you choose this specific component as your critical machinable part, and why this manufacturing process?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your justification directly, functional criticality, geometric complexity requiring precision machining, material considerations, and why 3-axis milling or 2-axis turning specifically suits it.
judge_qna.follow_up: What alternative manufacturing process did you consider and reject, and why?

judge_qna.question: How realistic is your CAM toolpath and manufacturing workflow, would this actually machine correctly?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Discuss your specific toolpath strategy, tool selection, and any real machinability constraints (tool access, fixturing) you accounted for, and be honest about any simplifications made for the challenge timeframe.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would need to change to make this genuinely production-ready?
